critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~6800 lines — refinement + forge training routes should be moved into a dedicated router module (repeated from iter 29/30). Not blocking.

POST /api/forge/training/refinements has no rate limit / abuse control. Since it's role-gated (admin+employee) risk is low, but a per-user daily cap (e.g. 200/day) would prevent accidental training-set flooding.
In InvestigationReport.jsx openRefine(), ai_original is only captured when engine==='ai'. Fine, but consider always storing the pre-edit narrative so audits work in offline mode too.

success_rate.frontend: 100% — auth-guard, prefill, submit, regression testids all verified

seed_data_creation: One TEST_iter31 refinement created via pytest is cleaned up in fixture teardown; one E2E-created refinement was manually deleted post-run. No residual test data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Correct localStorage token key for the frontend is 'nivx_token' (see /app/frontend/src/lib/auth.js) — NOT 'token' or 'nivx_admin_token'. Login endpoint returns {access_token, user{role}}. Refine dialog is inside <Dialog> from shadcn — use force=True when clicking submit. Investigation report auto-detects case_type; 'mixed' happens when both malware sha256 + IP indicators are present. Offline mode is fast and enough to exercise the Refine flow; AI mode adds ~10-15s. Backend endpoint /api/forge/training/refinements accepts both admin and employee roles and returns {ok, id, title, case_type, created_by, created_at}.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. First E2E attempt failed because tests wrote token to 'token'/'nivx_admin_token' keys while frontend reads 'nivx_token'; corrected in the re-run.
